prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian region terminal airspace near capacity; airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep local safety authority. System: Regional Flow Platform (alias Cedarbell), ATFM/A-CDM coordination layer; doesn't replace ATC, airport control rooms, airline ops centers, ground handling dispatch. Parts: Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. External: airline reservation, crew, baggage, commercial, national surveillance, avionics systems (authenticated, audited). Actors: Regional Flow Manager (primary), Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Slot Coordinator, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Handling Resource Planner, Deicing Coordinator, Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Items: Flight Intent Message, Airport Capacity Plan, Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, Airport Acceptance Rate, Tactical Regulation Proposal, Runway Inspection Note, Decision Log entries, Post Operations Report. Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. Requirements: stakeholders assign accountable reps, follow data rules, support post-op review; no binding Calculated Takeoff Times during baseline; post-approval changes only via controlled platform functions. Morning baseline (owner Regional Flow Manager): Flight Data Exchange normalizes schedules/Flight Intent Message; Demand Prediction Service builds demand profile; Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative (Business Rules Registry) validate; Meteorology Briefing Officer weather -> Weather Ingest Gateway -> Capacity Assessment Module; Military Airspace Liaison confirms airspace availability; Tower Supervisor sends Runway Inspection Note, declares runway config/constraints for Runway Meters; Airport Duty Manager confirms facilities; Ramp Control Lead reviews stands via Ramp Movement Board, Apron Sensors; Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms coverage; Handling Resource Planner flags turn-risk bands. Capacity Assessment Module proposes Airport

New part:
S075: Section 4 defines the accountable roles used after the approved morning baseline is distributed through the Regional Flow Platform.
S076: For role-call clarity, the Regional Flow Manager is also known as Copperfin during this deployment.
S077: During pre-tactical operations, the Regional Flow Manager owns the regional operating intent and confirms that planned demand, declared capacity, and coordination milestones are aligned.
S078: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the Airport Capacity Plan, the Ground Delay Program status, and any Tactical Regulation Proposal before they are presented for collaborative agreement.
S079: The Airspace Sector Planner supports the Regional Flow Manager by validating sector constraints in the Sector Load Monitor and by advising whether demand smoothing is required before tactical execution.
S080: The Slot Coordinator maintains accountability for Calculated Takeoff Time allocation policy and confirms that the Slot Allocation Engine applies the current Business Rules Registry parameters.
S081: The Airline Operations Coordinator represents carrier operating priorities and confirms that Flight Intent Message updates are complete, timely, and traceable.
S082: The Aircraft Operator Representative provides aircraft-specific constraints when requested and is responsible for ensuring that operator commitments entered in the Airport CDM Portal are operationally achievable.
S083: The Network Operations Liaison coordinates with adjacent network units and confirms that regional measures remain compatible with upstream and downstream flow constraints.
S084: The Network Operations Liaison also records external coordination outcomes in the Collaborative Decision Log so that later decisions can be reconstructed without relying on informal communications.
S085: The Meteorology Briefing Officer produces the Storm Cell Snapshot before the pre-tactical capacity review begins.
S086: The Meteorology Briefing Officer briefs forecast confidence, timing risk, and expected operational impact in the Digital Briefing Room using data supplied through the Weather Ingest Gateway.
S087: When forecast uncertainty is material, the Meteorology Briefing Officer states the trigger conditions that would justify moving from Normal Operations to Adverse Weather Mode.
S088: The Airport Duty Manager is the primary airport escalation contact and confirms that airport-side constraints are reflected consistently across the Airport CDM Portal and the Common Situation Display.
S089: The Tower Supervisor is accountable for tactical runway sequencing decisions and confirms that the Tower Sequence Manager reflects the current runway configuration.
S090: The Ramp Control Lead is accountable for apron movement coordination and maintains the Ramp Movement Board in a state that supports reliable departure metering.
S091: The Ground Handling Dispatcher confirms that handling resource assumptions are current in the Handling Resource Planner and escalates material deviations through the Airport Duty Manager.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
